model: U.S. Boiler Company Sage2 combustion controller via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: U.S. Boiler (Burnham) boilers with the Sage2 combustion controller on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Sage2 controller: 308 objects (303 AI, 5 AO), 53 polled by default. It reads supply, return, header, stack and outdoor sensors, commanded firing rate, fan speed, flame signal, active CH/DHW/lead-lag setpoints and operating points, burner control state, lockout, hold and alarm codes, demand and pump status. Five outputs are the resettable cycle and run-time counters.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile US_Boiler_SAGE2_COMB_Controller_a_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the Sage2 Modbus register list (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/Sage2.doc).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 53 of the 308 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.

integration.summary: Read burner control state, supply temperature against the active CH setpoint, firing rate and the lockout/hold/alarm codes. The profile does not write setpoints.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: The writable outputs are only the cycle and run-time counters; don't write them by accident.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
